author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty on either form
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory — the page and the machine-readable listing — can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty. The machine-readable form becomes a supported surface with this, its first capability.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable form is requested, then it carries every veterinarian with their specialties
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when either form is requested for that specialty, then only those veterinarians appear
given a specialty name differing from the held one only by letter case, when either form is requested, then it matches
given only the opening letters of a specialty's name, when either form is requested, then no veterinarian matches on them
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested, then the listing comes back with no veterinarian in it
given an empty or all-space specialty, when either form is requested, then every veterinarian is listed, as with no specialty at all
given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when the reader moves to another page, then the same specialty still applies
given a narrowed directory, when its pages are counted, then the count covers the narrowed list, not the whole directory
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing a specialty — the owner recorded on 2026-09-08 that a control may follow as its own request
free-text search for a veterinarian by name, and any search over pets or visits — NG-9 keeps these out
narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
notes: The machine-readable listing is reinstated under this fresh id; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn in the Superseded list and its id is not reused. Three open questions are recorded in the PRD rather than consulted on, per the intake's no-further-answer clause: a visible specialty control, whether an unknown specialty name differs from an unheld one, and whether the machine-readable form should be paged. Narrow readings taken: an unknown name behaves as an unheld one, and the machine-readable form stays a single document. The NG-9 narrowing is recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-08-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md. That ADR is not indexed in docs/adr/README.md — the index row is outside this agent's write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and needs no new module, layer, or dependency; it extends the existing controller-to-repository seam that docs/adr/2026-07-31-feature-package-organization.md records. Two points are genuinely new ground and are now recorded. First, the machine-readable veterinarian listing becomes a supported contract: docs/system-design.md Contracts now maps Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, and VetController to REQ-VET-003, and the Known Defects row calling that route requirement-less is retracted with a back-link to the non-goal ADR. Second, a caller-supplied value must not become a key in the unbounded, never-evicted vets cache; docs/adr/2026-09-08-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md decides that specialty-filtered reads bypass the cache while the unfiltered reads keep @Cacheable("vets") unchanged, and the VetRepository Contracts row carries the rule. Shape for the implementer: add one derived query, findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, in both a Page<Vet> (Pageable) and a Collection<Vet> form, neither annotated @Cacheable. VetController strips the optional specialty parameter and treats blank as absent, exactly as OwnerController:98-105 does for lastName, then dispatches to the filtered or unfiltered repository method. The JSON route stays a single unpaged document per the PRD's narrow reading. No page control is added: the intake pins the filter to a URL contract only.
integration_points: Repository boundary, query semantics: use the REAL VetRepository against H2 in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest, the project's existing real-repository home). Case-insensitive whole-name matching, a prefix matching nothing, an unheld name yielding an empty page, and the narrowed total count are repository truths and cannot be observed through a doubled repository.

Repository boundary, controller wiring: keep the @MockitoBean VetRepository already declared in VetControllerTests:51 rather than introducing a second doubling style in one file. The brief tolerates Mockito and does not encourage it (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy); a new doubled collaborator elsewhere reaches for a real implementation or a hand-written stub first.

Framework transport boundary: MockMvc in VetControllerTests, the one sanctioned mock (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy). It drives the real binding and dispatch machinery, so parameter binding and blank-value normalization are exercised for real.
HTML page: vetList.html gains the specialty on every pagination link so a narrowed page stays narrowed; VetController adds the normalized specialty to the model for the template to read.

patterns.description: Optional filter value stripped, blank read as the broadest search, then passed to a paged derived repository query. The specialty filter follows this shape.

Derived query naming the restriction in the method name. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase follows it; no @Query string is needed and none should be written (security-principles.md Realization, injection row).

risks.risk: Splicing the specialty into a Thymeleaf link expression the way the current pagination links splice the page number (vetList.html:30, the @{'...__${i}__'} preprocessing form) evaluates caller-supplied text as expression source and emits it unencoded.
risks.mitigation: Every pagination link uses the parameterized link-expression form, @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value and never preprocesses it. Note that ownersList.html is NOT a usable precedent: it drops lastName from its page links entirely, so there is no adjacent seam to copy. security-principles.md Realization, cross-site-scripting row.

risks.risk: specialties.name carries no unique constraint in any vendor schema, so two rows sharing a name would join a vet twice and corrupt both the page contents and the total count.
risks.mitigation: Derive the query with findDistinctBy..., which emits select distinct and count(distinct). Acceptance criterion 8 (the count covers the narrowed list) is the assertion that catches a regression.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is an EAGER @ManyToMany, and the filtered query adds a restriction join over that same collection while paging it.
risks.mitigation: The existing findAll(Pageable) already pages this mapping, so the fetch strategy is unchanged; assert it rather than assume it, with a multi-page narrowed dataset covering acceptance criteria 7 and 8.

risks.risk: Caching the filtered read would let any unauthenticated caller mint cache entries in a cache with no size limit and no expiry (CacheConfiguration builds it from a bare MutableConfiguration; Open Questions from the Survey, item 5).
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on either filtered method, per docs/adr/2026-09-08-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md. security-principles.md Trust Boundaries, least-privilege row.

notes: ADR index row requested in the dispatch is added, along with a row for the new cache ADR; docs/adr/README.md is within this agent's write scope. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Effort rated involved: the pagination-link rework has no safe precedent in the codebase, the slice spans two representations, and seven named tests split across two test classes with different doubling strategies. The three open questions the PRD records (a visible control, unknown versus unheld specialty names, paging the machine-readable form) need no design decision here; the narrow readings the PRD took are consistent with this block.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain check not run and therefore not clean: the project configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin (no dependencyCheck in build.gradle), and this reviewer has no network access, so nothing in this slice was matched against the NVD. Declared versions read from build.gradle: Spring Boot 4.1.1, dependency-management 1.1.7, GraalVM buildtools 1.1.2, CycloneDX 3.4.1. Jackson and Thymeleaf resolve transitively through the Boot BOM. The dependency set is unchanged by this slice, so this is a standing CI/human item rather than a property of the change.

Name shadowing with a latent security edge in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html: the table body binds a loop variable also called specialty (th:each="specialty : ${vet.specialties}"), which shadows the model attribute of the same name inside that span. Today the five pagination links sit outside that scope, so they resolve the model attribute as intended and the rendered output is correct. The hazard is for the next editor: a link added inside the table that writes specialty=${specialty} would silently bind the Specialty entity instead of the filter value. Renaming the loop variable (for example to held) would remove the ambiguity. Not a defect in this change; raised so the code-quality reviewer and a future editor see it.

The specialty parameter carries no explicit maximum length. Reach is limited: the value is matched by equality in a bound parameter, the servlet container already caps request-line and header size, and the neighbouring owner last-name search accepts unbounded text the same way, so this change is consistent with the codebase's existing boundary handling rather than weaker than it. Noted only as the one input-validation dimension the change leaves open.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty reaches persistence only as a bound parameter of the Spring Data derived query VetRepository.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase (Collection and Page forms). No string-concatenated query text, no @Query, no JPQL fragment built from request-derived text. Grep over src/main/java for concatenation into query text and for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec returns nothing new.

Cross-site scripting: the request-derived value is rendered nowhere as text. Its only appearance in vets/vetList.html is as a query-parameter value inside five th:href link expressions of the form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value and then HTML-escapes the attribute. Grep for th:utext, th:inline, and javascript: across src/main/resources/templates returns nothing.

Template-expression injection improved over baseline: all five pagination links moved off the @{'...__${x}__'} preprocessing form. Preprocessing evaluates its content as expression source, so carrying a reader-supplied specialty through it would have been an SpEL-evaluation surface; the parameterized form has no such property. This is a net reduction of the change's own surface, not merely a neutral rewrite.

Cache poisoning / unbounded cache growth avoided by construction: neither filtered read carries @Cacheable, and the reason (a cache key derived from caller-supplied text against a 'vets' cache with no size limit or expiry) is recorded both inline in VetRepository and in docs/adr/2026-09-08-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md. Adding @Cacheable there would have been a reachable memory-exhaustion vector for any anonymous caller.
Mass assignment: no new request-bound type or WebDataBinder. Both handlers take a scalar @RequestParam String, so the identifier-binding disallow rule in docs/security-principles.md is not engaged.
Concurrency: VetController stays a stateless singleton. normalizeSpecialty is static and pure; no mutable field, collection, or non-thread-safe formatter is introduced.

Null and error handling: @RequestParam(defaultValue = "") makes the parameter non-null before strip(), so no unchecked dereference. No new exception message, log line, or rendered value carries request-derived or internal detail, so the error-disclosure row of the threat model is untouched.

No new endpoint, no broadened actuator exposure, no credential, secret, file, path, shell, XML, or deserialization surface introduced. Grep for hardcoded-secret names over the diff returns only the test constants RADIOLOGY/RADIOLOGISTS naming domain data.

Supply chain: scripts/changeset.sh --name-only shows no build.gradle or lockfile change, so the resolved dependency set is unchanged by this slice and no new artifact needed the four checks in system-design.md.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow both vet-directory surfaces by an optional specialty parameter

blast_radius.note: Ten files but one module: the whole code delta sits in the vet package (VetController, VetRepository, vetList.html) with no sensitive path, no config, no build or dependency change, and nothing touched in owner, pet, or visit code. The five doc files carry real reach — the PRD narrows non-goal NG-9 and reinstates the machine-readable listing as a supported surface — but each edit transcribes the owner's recorded intake decision rather than a scope claim the slice invented.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: normalizeSpecialty only strips, the repository does the case folding through IgnoreCase, and both dispatches branch on isEmpty() so a blank value takes the identical unfiltered path as before — no boundary flipped, no operator inverted. One ripple the requirement does not mention and no test pins: the pagination links moved to the parameterized link form, so an unfiltered page now renders a trailing empty specialty= in all five links where it previously rendered none. Cosmetic only, since the controller reads an empty value as absent, and the same rewrite is what takes the reader-supplied value out of Thymeleaf's expression-preprocessing form.

test_adequacy.note: The tests are real rather than tautological and split at the right seam: query semantics (whole-name case-insensitive match, a prefix matching nothing, an empty result, page count over the narrowed list, page two staying narrowed) run against a real VetRepository on H2 in ClinicServiceTests, while blank-value normalization, link carry-over, and encoding of a specialty carrying URL syntax run through MockMvc. Each would fail against a broken implementation. One blemish to see: VetControllerTests names a constant A_SPECIALTY_NO_VET_HOLDS with the value dentistry, but the H2 seed gives dentistry to Douglas — the test still holds because the repository is stubbed there, yet the name encodes a false premise about the fixture.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four planned reviewers approved, but two approvals carry residue. The security reviewer approved with three recommendations, one of them a latent trap in a file this change edits: vetList.html binds a loop variable also named specialty over vet.specialties in the table body, so a page link ever added inside that scope would silently bind the Specialty entity instead of the filter value — correct today only because the five links sit outside the loop. Its other two notes are that no supply-chain scan was run and that the parameter carries no maximum length. Separately, the test-reviewer's round-two approval justifies the fix by stating that dentistry is a specialty no vet holds in the seed data, which the seed contradicts.

scope_deviation.note: Zero design revisions, zero consultations, one build retry, and every changed path was named in advance by the design-block's primary or supporting paths. The change stops where the intake pinned it: a URL contract with no form or dropdown, the machine-readable listing left unpaged, and the three genuinely open choices recorded as PRD open questions rather than decided in code.

rationale: Two approvals carry residue worth a human's eyes before merge: the security reviewer's template-shadowing hazard on the specialty name inside vetList.html, and the test-reviewer's round-two justification that dentistry is held by no vet, which the H2 seed contradicts.
